deck_title: Kelvin-Laplace capillary-gravity wave dispersion vs naive gravity-only sluggish ripple rig

cards.subtitle: Deterministic William Thomson (Lord Kelvin, 1871) & Thomas Young (1805) / Pierre-Simon Laplace (1806) capillary-gravity wave dispersion relation (omega^2 = g*k + (gamma/rho)*k^3 = g*k*(1 + u) where inverse Bond number u = (gamma*k^2)/(rho*g) in [0.0000, 1.0000], locking normalized wave period-squared ratio at T^2/T_exact^2 = 1.0000x across all 17 wavenumber stations with 0/17 sluggish stations) versus naive pure-gravity dispersion (omega^2 = g*k, which omits Young-Laplace surface-tension curvature restoring pressure and bloats wave period-squared as 1 + u to 1.2500x at u=0.25, 1.5000x at u=0.50, and 2.0000x at the 1.73 cm capillary-gravity crossover u=1.00 across 16/17 stations) and 64-layer Airy velocity-potential vertical quadrature.
